exposure: PEA POD(tm) neonatal body fat percentage (BF%)
Skinfold measurements (triceps and subscapular) for BF%
cohort: The study included 149 neonates who had their body fat percentage prospectively estimated.
finding: Neonatal body fat percentage (BF%), estimated by either PEA POD(tm) or skinfold measurements, performs better to predict neonatal hypothermia than birthweight centile, and skinfold measurements offer an inexpensive alternative to PEA POD(tm).
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken prospectively after birth, with medical record review for subsequent hypothermic episodes.
birth_weight: Customized birthweight centiles were calculated, and 'birthweight <10th centile' was used as a classification.
